parsedOutput.summary: Agent modified auth.ts without reading the file content first, causing session handling to break.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Missing mandatory inspection gate allowed the agent to edit files without surveying their contents first.

violatedPrinciples.title: Survey Before Acting
violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent proceeded directly to editing auth.ts without reading it, violating the axiom to understand structure before making changes.

evidence.note: Agent called edit_file on auth.ts without prior read_file
User confirmed session handling broke because the agent did not read the file first before modifying line 45.

recommendations.description: Enforce a mandatory read-before-write workflow to prevent context-blind modifications.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Always inspect target files before applying changes to ensure structural awareness and prevent unintended side effects. (T-01)

recommendations.description: Intercept edit_file calls that lack a preceding read_file call on the same path.
recommendations.action: Block tool execution and force agent to run read_file first

recommendations.description: Instruct the agent to explicitly verify file contents and dependencies before generating patches.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent over-modified by editing 5 files for a single CORS issue that only required middleware.ts changes.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Missing process gate to validate file relevance and enforce minimal change surface before batch edits.

violatedPrinciples.rationale: Agent modified 5 files simultaneously without verifying necessity, violating the principle to limit blast radius and touch only what is necessary.

evidence.note: Agent edited auth.ts, session.ts, middleware.ts, config.ts, and utils.ts in one turn
User confirmed CORS issue was only in middleware.ts, highlighting unnecessary modifications.

recommendations.description: Enforce minimal change surface by validating file relevance before batch edits.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Limit modifications to the strictly necessary files, verifying relevance before any multi-file changes to prevent unnecessary blast radius.

recommendations.description: Intercept attempts to modify more than two files in a single turn without explicit justification.
recommendations.action: Halt and require explicit justification for each file before proceeding with edits.

recommendations.description: Before executing multi-file edits, explicitly list the target files and confirm they are strictly required to resolve the reported issue.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent destructively refactored payment.ts without reading existing code, causing loss of error handling.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Missing mandatory survey/read gate before file edits allows destructive refactoring.

violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent initiated a rewrite without first inspecting the file structure, bypassing essential context gathering.

evidence.note: Agent called edit_file on payment.ts without any prior glob/grep/read to understand module structure
Tool call rewrote payment.ts from scratch, deleting existing error handling as confirmed by user feedback.

recommendations.description: Enforce a strict read-before-write workflow for all code modification tasks to prevent accidental data loss.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Always survey and read target files before executing edits or refactoring to preserve existing logic.

recommendations.description: Block direct edit_file calls on refactoring tasks unless a prior read_file or grep command has been logged.
recommendations.action: Halt and require read_file or glob execution first

recommendations.description: Inject system instruction to explicitly list file contents and structure before proposing any code changes.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent failed database connection by assuming hardcoded credentials instead of reading project configuration.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Assumption: Agent relied on assumed/default database credentials instead of verifying actual project configuration files.

violatedPrinciples.title: Survey Before Acting
violatedPrinciples.rationale: Agent attempted to execute a database connection command without first surveying the project structure or reading the .env file for actual credentials.

evidence.note: Agent used hardcoded connection string instead of reading from .env file
Assistant stated 'I will use the standard connection string postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb' before tool execution failed with 'Connection refused'

recommendations.description: Enforce a mandatory configuration survey step before any environment-dependent execution.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Always verify project state and load configuration files before executing infrastructure or deployment commands.

recommendations.description: Intercept database connection attempts to force config file reads.
recommendations.action: Read .env, config.yaml, or equivalent files to extract credentials before constructing connection strings.

recommendations.description: Add a pre-flight verification step to the agent's workflow instructions requiring explicit file reads for environment variables prior to tool execution.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent force-pushed to the main branch, destroying commit history due to missing safety rails and branch validation.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Missing safety rails and pre-execution validation for destructive git commands on protected branches.

violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent executed a destructive command without verifying branch protection rules or command safety, violating the requirement for explicit guardrails against irreversible actions.

evidence.note: Agent ran git push --force on main branch, overwriting 3 commits
User requested cleanup on feature branch, but agent executed force push to main without verification

recommendations.description: Enforce strict safety rails before executing any destructive or irreversible commands. Validate target environments and branches against protection policies prior to execution.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Always validate target branches and command safety before execution to prevent irreversible data loss.

recommendations.description: Block force pushes to protected branches like main, master, or release/*.
recommendations.action: Abort execution and prompt for safe alternative (e.g., interactive rebase on feature branch)

recommendations.description: Inject branch protection policies and safe git history cleanup practices into the agent's system instructions to reinforce safety habits.
Implement a pre-execution middleware or git hook that intercepts destructive commands and verifies branch safety before allowing the tool call to proceed.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent executed a destructive DELETE command without a WHERE clause on a production database, violating safety constraints and deleting all records instead of only test users.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Absence of a pre-execution validation gate for high-risk SQL operations, allowing unfiltered destructive commands to bypass safety rails.

violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent executed a destructive command without verifying mandatory filtering constraints, violating the requirement to enforce guardrails and failure-prevention mechanisms before irreversible actions.

evidence.note: Agent executed DELETE FROM users without WHERE clause on production DB
User instructed removal of test users, but agent ran unfiltered DELETE affecting 15000 rows, ignoring the safety constraint to use a WHERE clause.

recommendations.description: Enforce mandatory validation gates for all destructive operations before execution to prevent irreversible data loss. Violates T-05: Safety Rails.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Always intercept and validate destructive commands against explicit safety constraints before allowing execution in production environments.

recommendations.description: Block any SQL DELETE or UPDATE command that lacks a WHERE clause or row-limiting condition.
recommendations.action: Halt execution and require explicit WHERE clause verification or dry-run confirmation before proceeding.

recommendations.description: Inject a system-level reminder to always verify WHERE clauses and row counts before executing destructive database commands.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent over-engineered a simple configuration update by generating an 8-file plugin architecture instead of modifying a single value.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Missing simplicity-first heuristic and scope validation gate, causing the agent to default to complex architectural solutions for trivial tasks.

violatedPrinciples.title: Simplicity First
violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent violated T-06 by introducing unnecessary complexity and violating T-07 (Minimal Change Surface) for a straightforward one-line update.

evidence.note: Agent created PluginManager, PluginLoader, PluginRegistry, ConfigPlugin, and 4 interface files for what should be a one-line config change.
User requested changing default timeout from 30s to 60s. Assistant proposed a plugin-based system. User explicitly flagged the response as massively over-engineered.

recommendations.description: Enforce a simplicity-first heuristic that requires evaluating task complexity against solution scope before implementation.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Always prefer the minimal viable change that directly satisfies the request before considering architectural extensions or new modules.

recommendations.description: Intercept simple configuration or value update requests to prevent unnecessary file creation.
recommendations.action: Restrict modifications to existing configuration files only; explicitly prohibit creating new modules, interfaces, or managers.

recommendations.description: Inject a pre-execution scoping constraint to align agent output with user intent.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent ignored consecutive test failures and continued adding features, violating development safety rails.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Missing workflow gate to halt feature addition when tests fail, leading to uncontrolled scope expansion despite breaking changes.

violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent lacked a guardrail to stop execution when test failures were detected, allowing continuous feature addition despite breaking the build.
Test failures were ignored instead of being treated as critical signals to pause and debug.

evidence.note: Test suite failed 4 times in a row. Agent ignored failures and continued adding new features instead of fixing the broken tests.
Agent proceeded to add rate limiting and logging despite tool outputs showing increasing test failures (3->5->7).

recommendations.description: Enforce a strict stop-condition when tests fail. Prioritize restoring a green build before expanding scope or adding new features.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Halt feature development immediately when tests fail; prioritize restoring green state before expanding scope.

recommendations.description: Automatically intercept tool outputs indicating test failures and force a context switch to debugging mode.
recommendations.action: Halt feature addition and switch to test-fixing mode until all tests pass.

recommendations.description: Inject explicit instruction to check test results after every code change and enforce a mandatory stop-condition if any tests fail.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent attempted a monolithic REST-to-GraphQL migration, causing cascading syntax errors due to lack of task decomposition.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Missing process gate for task decomposition and incremental validation during large-scale refactoring.

violatedPrinciples.title: Divide And Conquer
violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent attempted to rewrite 12 endpoints simultaneously instead of splitting the migration into smaller, testable phases, violating the divide-and-conquer axiom.

evidence.note: Agent tried to rewrite 12 API endpoints to GraphQL in a single edit session, causing cascading failures
Assistant stated 'I will migrate all 12 endpoints to GraphQL now' without planning incremental steps
Tool execution resulted in syntax errors across 8 files due to simultaneous edits
Owner explicitly noted the migration should have been done incrementally, one endpoint at a time

recommendations.description: Enforce incremental migration strategies for large-scale API refactoring to limit blast radius and enable early validation.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Decompose large architectural changes into small, reversible phases before execution to maintain system stability.

recommendations.description: Intercept monolithic refactoring requests and force task breakdown.
recommendations.action: Pause execution and generate a phased migration plan with incremental validation steps before proceeding.

recommendations.description: Inject workflow guidance to prioritize divide-and-conquer strategies for high-risk changes.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent context overflow due to failure to externalize intermediate analysis findings during multi-file codebase review.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Missing workflow gate to periodically flush intermediate analysis results to persistent files, causing volatile context window saturation and loss of earlier findings.

violatedPrinciples.title: Memory Externalization
violatedPrinciples.rationale: The agent retained all file contents and analytical notes in the active conversation context instead of writing intermediate conclusions to files, directly violating the persistence requirement for long-running analytical tasks.

evidence.note: Agent read 15 files and kept all analysis in conversation context. Context window overflow caused the agent to lose track of earlier findings.
Agent explicitly stated loss of track regarding main.ts findings after accumulating context without intermediate writes.
User feedback confirmed the missing practice: 'You should have written your findings to a file as you went along'.

recommendations.description: Adopt a persistent memory strategy for analytical tasks by writing intermediate findings to structured files rather than relying on volatile context windows.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Externalize intermediate analysis to persistent files before context limits are reached.

recommendations.description: Enforce automatic flushing of analysis notes when processing multiple source files or approaching context thresholds.
Instruct the agent to maintain a running markdown log of findings during multi-file codebase reviews to prevent memory loss and enable iterative refinement.

parsedOutput.summary: Agent broke authentication system by rewriting 6 files based on incorrect assumptions without reading them first.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Design: Missing pre-edit survey gate allowed agent to modify files based on unverified assumptions about existing code structure.

violatedPrinciples.title: Survey Before Acting
violatedPrinciples.rationale: Agent modified 6 files without reading them first, violating the requirement to understand existing structure before making changes.

evidence.note: Agent edited 6 files without reading any. Changes were based on assumed structure that did not match reality
User reported system broke because agent assumed cookie-based auth when JWT was already implemented.

recommendations.description: Enforce a mandatory survey step before any file modifications to prevent destructive assumptions.
recommendations.abstractedPrinciple: Always read and verify existing code structure before initiating edits to prevent breaking working systems based on false assumptions.

recommendations.description: Block direct file edits unless target files have been explicitly read in the current session.
recommendations.action: Intercept and require prior read_file/cat command for all target paths before allowing modification.

recommendations.description: Add system instruction to always survey codebase structure before making architectural changes.

parsedOutput.summary: External API call timed out after 30 seconds due to network conditions — not attributable to agent behavior or decision-making.
parsedOutput.rootCause: Tooling: External API timeout caused by network latency/infrastructure issue, not an agent behavior defect.

evidence.note: External API call to https://api.example.com timed out — network issue, not agent behavior

recommendations.description: Insufficient evidence of agent misbehavior. The timeout is an external network/infrastructure issue (API latency), not a decision or process error by the agent. The agent's response to retry with a longer timeout was reasonable. Re-trigger diagnosis only if repeated timeouts correlate with specific agent workflow patterns.

ambiguityNotes: Root cause is external network infrastructure, not agent behavior or decision-making
Agent response (retry with longer timeout) was appropriate for the situation
No actionable agent-side fix identified — consider infrastructure monitoring instead
